chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ayoub ibn Yaqteen, or someone else from them (peace be upon him).
The supplication for the last ten (nights): You should say on the first night,

O He who causes the entry of the night into the day, and the entry of the day into the night, and the Extractor of the living from the dead, and the Extractor of the dead from the living! O Sustainer of whom He wills without measure! O Allah, O Beneficent, O Allah, O Merciful, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah! For You are the Beautiful Names, and the Exalted Examples, and the Greatness, and the Loftiness!

I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his Family, and to make my name in this night among the fortunate, and my soul with the martyrs, and my good deeds in 'Illiyin, and my bad deeds forgiven.

And to grant me conviction with which my heart is gladdened, and faith which removes doubt from me, and to please me with what You have apportioned for me, and give us good in the world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the punishment of the fire, and grant us therein Your remembrance, and Your gratitude, and hopefulness to You, and return, and success for what You succeeded Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) in.

And you should say on the second night: O He who brings forth the day from the night, so we are in darkness, and the Mover of the sun to its resting place by Your decree! O Mighty, O Knowing, and the Ordainer of the moon's phases until it returns like the old palm branch! O Light of every light, and the destination of every hope, and the Guardian of every blessing! O Allah, O Beneficent, O Allah, O Holy, O One, O Alone, O Solitary, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah! For You are the Beautiful Names and the Exalted Examples.
Then you return to the first supplication up to his words: 'I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and his Family,' up to the end of the supplication.

And you should say on the third night: O Lord of the Night of Decree, and the Maker of it better than a thousand months, and Lord of the night and the day, and the mountains and the seas, and the darknesses and the lights, and the earth and the sky! O Creator, O Fashioner, O Affectionate, O Benefactor, O Allah, O Beneficent, O Allah, O Eternal, O Allah, O Initiator, O Allah, O Allah, O Allah! For You are the Beautiful Names and the Exalted Examples, and the Greatness, and the Loftiness.

I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, and to make my name in this night among the fortunate, and my soul with the martyrs, and my good deeds in 'Illiyin, and my bad deeds forgiven.

And to grant me conviction with which my heart is gladdened, and faith which removes doubt from me, and to please me with what You have apportioned for me, and give us good in the world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the punishment of the fire, and grant me therein Your remembrance, and Your gratitude, and hopefulness to You, and return, and repentance, and success for what You succeeded Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him) in.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications to recite on the first three nights of the last ten days of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* prescribes the *Du'a al-Akhir* (Supplication of the Last Ten Nights), a cornerstone of Shia Ramadan devotion that emphasizes *Tajalli* (divine manifestation) through specific attributes like *Al-Mulij* (The Introducer) and *Al-Salih* (The Exiter). The structure reflects the theological progression from cosmic order to the specific blessings of *Laylat al-Qadr*, culminating in a comprehensive petition for *Yaqeen* (certainty) and entry among the *Sa'ida* (the fortunate).
